name: Anterior (ventral) horn
summary: The motor part of the spinal gray matter. It contains the alpha motor neurons that innervate skeletal muscle (the lower motor neurons), the gamma motor neurons for muscle spindles, and the interneurons, including Renshaw cells, that shape their output. Motor neurons are arranged somatotopically: medial groups supply axial muscles, lateral groups the limbs (present only in the enlargements), with flexors dorsal to extensors. Their death, as in poliomyelitis, spinal muscular atrophy and motor neuron disease, produces the lower motor neuron picture of weakness, wasting, fasciculations and lost reflexes.

anatomy.location: Anterior part of the gray matter on each side, largest in the cervical and lumbosacral enlargements where the lateral motor columns for the limbs are added to the medial columns for the trunk.

subdivisions.name: Medial motor column
subdivisions.note: axial and trunk muscles, all levels

subdivisions.name: Lateral motor column
subdivisions.note: limb muscles, C5–T1 and L2–S3; proximal muscles medial, distal muscles lateral

subdivisions.name: Onuf's nucleus
subdivisions.note: S2–S4, external urethral and anal sphincters; spared in motor neuron disease

function: Final common pathway for movement: integrates corticospinal, brainstem and segmental reflex inputs into the firing of motor units; gamma neurons set spindle sensitivity and muscle tone.

bestView.label: anterior gray horns of the upper cervical cord

imaging.normalAppearance: The anterior horns are the anterior limbs of the gray butterfly on axial T2 at high resolution; bilateral anterior horn T2 hyperintensity (owl's eyes or snake eyes) is seen in cord infarction, compressive myelopathy and viral anterior horn infection.

pathology.finding: Bilateral anterior horn T2 hyperintensity (owl's eyes) with restricted diffusion.
Longitudinal T2 hyperintensity confined to the anterior gray matter.
Normal cord imaging; the diagnosis is clinical and electrophysiological.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Axial T2 of the cord; EMG for denervation

lesionEffects.deficit: Flaccid weakness, wasting, fasciculations, absent reflexes in the affected myotomes
lesionEffects.mechanism: Lower motor neuron loss at the segment

lesionEffects.deficit: Asymmetric limb weakness without sensory loss
lesionEffects.mechanism: Pure motor gray matter disease (polio, SMA, ALS)

examination: Inspect for wasting and fasciculations at rest
Sensory testing (normal in pure anterior horn disease)
pearls: Weakness with wasting and fasciculations but normal sensation is anterior horn disease
Upper motor neuron signs in the legs with lower motor neuron signs in the arms and no sensory loss: motor neuron disease
